meta.title: About
meta.description: Why Layangin exists, what it simulates, what it deliberately does not do, and who built it.

header.title: A kite duel, taken seriously
header.lead: Layangin is a small browser game about one specific thing: the moment two kite lines cross and one of them gives.

why.title: Why this game
why.body: Kite fighting is one of the few games where the whole contest happens through a piece of string. Most kite games skip that and turn it into a dodging game. Layangin does the opposite: the line is the entire mechanic — its tension, its sag, where it crosses, and how fast it is sliding.

simulated.title: What is simulated
items: Wind that increases with altitude following the standard power-law profile, with gusts generated as fractal noise.
Thin-plate aerodynamics: lift and drag computed from the sail's angle of attack against the apparent wind.
A flying line that sags as a shallow catenary when slack, goes straight under load, and parts if held past its breaking tension.
Abrasion at every crossing, weighted by sliding speed, contact pressure, crossing angle and which line is tauter.
Arena hazards: solid structures the kite collides with, steel cables that abrade a line without taking damage back, and wind shadows behind tall buildings where lift collapses.

notSimulated.title: What is not simulated
notSimulated.lead: Stated plainly, so the game is not mistaken for something it is not.
items: It is a 2D side-on view. Real kite duels happen in three dimensions and the wind window is a hemisphere, not an arc.
The kite's attitude is set by the bridle geometry rather than solved as a full rigid body with rotational inertia.
Line stretch, line weight distribution along its length, and line-on-line friction heating are approximated, not modelled.
The numbers are tuned for a readable 90-second match, not calibrated against measurements of real kites.
Lives are a game convention, not physics. A real cut line ends the flight; here it costs one of three lives so a duel is decided over several exchanges.

Kites are drawn about four and a half times larger than life. At true scale a 1 m sail on a 60 m line is a couple of pixels; collision and aerodynamics use the real size, only the drawing is exaggerated.

cultural.title: About the kites
cultural.body: The airframes are based on real Indonesian kite traditions — the Javanese pecut and sawangan, the Balinese bebean and janggan — alongside two modern shapes. They are interpretations for a game, not accurate reconstructions, and the game is not affiliated with any kite club, festival or organisation.
cultural.note: If something here misrepresents a tradition you know well, please say so — see the contact page.

framework.def: Nuxt with Vue and TypeScript, rendered mostly as static pages.

render.def: The arena is a 2D canvas drawn from a fixed-timestep simulation running at 120 Hz. Sound is synthesized with the Web Audio API — there are no audio files.

state.def: Pinia stores, with progress persisted to your browser's local storage.

i18n.def: English and Indonesian, with all interface text in translation files.

hosting.def: No backend. Nothing you do is sent anywhere.

author.title: Who made it
author.body: Built by {name} as a side project. Bug reports, corrections and ideas are all welcome.

meta.title: Contact
meta.description: Reach the developer of Layangin by email for bug reports, corrections or questions.

header.title: Say something
header.lead: One person maintains this. Email is the only channel, and it is read.

email.label: Email
email.name: Maulana Yusup A
email.note: No contact form, no phone line, no chat widget — an email address is the whole thing.

expect.title: What to expect
items: This is a side project, so replies are not guaranteed and may take a while.
Bug reports are much easier to act on with your browser, device and what you were doing at the time.
There is no account system, so there is nothing to recover if you clear your browser storage.

good.title: Especially useful
items: A match that behaved in a way the rules do not explain.
A control scheme that does not work on your device.
A translation that reads wrong in Indonesian.
Anything about the kites or terminology that a flyer would call incorrect.

contact.privacyNote: An email tells me your address and whatever you write. It is not added to any list and nothing is sent back to you except a reply.

meta.title: Compliance
meta.description: Accessibility, data handling, monetisation and content statements for Layangin, with what is verified and what is not.

header.title: What this site does and does not do
header.lead: Written to be checkable. Where something has not been formally tested, it says so instead of claiming a standard.

collection.def: None. There is no account system, no analytics, no tracking pixels and no third-party scripts.

storage.term: What is stored on your device
storage.def: Game progress (coins, owned airframes, liveries, colourways and effects, upgrade levels, ladder position, chosen arena) and your preferences, in your browser's local storage. A single cookie remembers your language choice.

transmission.def: Nothing from gameplay. Pages and fonts are downloaded from the host when you load the site; fonts are served from the same origin, not from a third party.

deletion.def: Use "Reset progress" in the shop, or clear site data in your browser. Since nothing is stored on a server, that is a complete deletion.

children.def: The game has no chat, no user-generated content, no purchases and no data collection, so there is nothing collected from any visitor regardless of age.

purchases.def: None. There is no store, no currency pack, no subscription and no payment processing anywhere in this project.

coins.def: Earned by playing only. They cannot be bought and have no value outside the game. Arenas are not purchasable at all — they unlock by win count.

chance.def: None. Every price is fixed and every item is bought directly.

cosmetic.def: Colourways, sail liveries and trail effects do not touch the simulation. None of them can change a match result — only airframes and upgrades affect how a kite flies, and both state their numbers before you buy.

ai.term: How the AI is made harder
ai.def: Only through human-shaped limits — reaction time, aim precision, stamina discipline and mistake rate — plus the gear it flies, which you can also buy. It reads the same state you can see.

upgrades.def: Each one multiplies a value the physics model already uses, and the multiplier is shown before you buy.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.lead: The target is WCAG 2.2 level AA. This has not been independently audited, so the list below separates what is implemented from what is known to fall short.
done: Keyboard operation throughout, including the whole match — no pointer is required to play.
Visible focus indicators on every interactive element, never removed.
A skip link to the main content on every page.
Semantic landmarks and headings in document order.
Live match readings duplicated as text next to the arena, so the canvas is not the only source of that information.
prefers-reduced-motion respected: page transitions, decorative animation and match particles all stop.
prefers-contrast: more strengthens borders and secondary text.
forced-colors support: decorative layers are dropped so system colours win.
Text and spacing sized in rem, so browser font-size settings scale the whole interface.
Touch targets of at least 44 px on the controls.
Sound is optional and can be switched off, and no information is conveyed by sound alone — every audio cue has a visible counterpart in the HUD or the round banner.
A lost line costs one life rather than the match, so a single mistimed input or an unlucky gust never ends a duel outright.
gaps: The arena itself is a canvas. It has a text alternative and text read-outs, but a fast duel is not a good experience with a screen reader.
The game requires reacting inside roughly a second, and there is currently no slow-motion or extended-time mode.
Colour is used alongside labels to distinguish the two fighters; the pairing has not been verified for every form of colour vision deficiency.
No formal audit or assistive-technology test matrix has been run. Reports of problems are genuinely useful.

cultural.def: Kite shapes and terminology are interpretations of Indonesian kite traditions for a game. No affiliation with, or endorsement by, any club, festival or organisation is claimed.

safety.def: Abrasive kite line is dangerous in reality. The how-to-play page says so directly rather than treating it as a game mechanic only.

assets.def: All kite artwork is generated in code from the geometry in this repository, and every sound is synthesized in the browser from oscillators and noise. No third-party images or audio files are used, and none are downloaded.

report.title: Report a problem
report.body: If any statement on this page is wrong, or you hit an accessibility barrier, email {email} and it will be corrected here.
